title: When Asking for Advice Is the Highest Form of Respect
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article makes the case that asking someone for advice is less about the information gained than about signaling that their views matter. It specifically highlights the amplified effect of asking for advice publicly — in front of peers, colleagues, or friends — rather than privately. Doing so, the author argues, broadcasts respect for that person to everyone within earshot, which can be more meaningful than the advice itself. The piece includes sample phrasing leaders can use to request counsel in a way that visibly elevates the person being asked, and frames this as a low-cost, high-impact relational habit with essentially no downside.
points: Asking for advice signals respect and value to the person being asked, regardless of the advice's content.
Asking for advice in front of others amplifies the relational impact far beyond a private request.
Leaders who seek counsel from those they respect model openness and smart thinking.
Public requests for advice broadcast the asker's regard for that person to everyone present.
The author frames this as an easy, low-risk habit for making people feel more valued.
quotes: Asking others for their advice and views on issues we are thinking about or struggling with is a sign of respect.
That’s why asking your leader for their perspective and advice on just about any matter important to you creates a deeper connection with them.
Great leaders take this idea one step further. They ask for that advice when others are present.
The gesture says loudly to anyone within earshot that you highly prize the views of this person.
Asking anyone for their advice and perspective is a good idea, but asking for that counsel in the presence of others is a great idea!
